title: GauSPU: 3D Gaussian Splatting Processor for Real-Time SLAM Systems
problem: Existing 3DGS-based SLAM systems suffer from inadequate tracking throughput due to expensive volume rendering with recursive ray-casting and irregular memory access patterns during gradient backpropagation. These computational and memory bottlenecks prevent real-time pose tracking.
motivation: 3D Gaussian Splatting enables rapid rendering and high-fidelity reconstruction for robotics and 3D vision, but existing systems cannot achieve real-time SLAM performance.
method: GauSPU uses sparse-tile-sampling to focus computation on informative image regions during pose tracking. A sparsity-adaptive ray recursion unit (SA-RRU) accelerates volume rendering by exploiting irregular spatial sparsity through sub-tile-wise execution and Morton-based thread allocation. A memory-access-relaxed backpropagation engine (MAR-BE) with gradient buffer and pose backward units eliminates atomic operations through coalescing and pipeline fusion.
key_novelty: Sparsity-adaptive ray recursion unit that exploits irregular spatial sparsity in volume rendering through Morton-ordered thread allocation and sub-tile-wise execution patterns.
contributions: Sparse-tile-sampling (STS) algorithm for efficient pose tracking in 3DGS-SLAM
Sparsity-adaptive ray recursion unit (SA-RRU) with sub-tile execution and Morton-based thread allocation for accelerated volume rendering
Memory-access-relaxed backpropagation engine (MAR-BE) with gradient coalescing and pipeline-fused backward propagation
Algorithm-hardware co-designed accelerator achieving 33.6 FPS real-time performance with 63.9x energy efficiency improvement
